taxonomy_note: Workflow routing only. Choose final root-cause taxonomy from supported evidence.

controls.boundary: Lambda Function URL authentication and application authorization
controls.source_trace: Identify whether public invocation is intended and which protected action the handler performs. Distinguish IAM URL admission from per-user/object authorization inside the function.
controls.implementation_branch: Resolve AuthType and the applicable URL permission model. For URLs subject to the October 2025 requirements, evaluate both lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl and lambda:InvokeFunction; one allow is insufficient. Under AWS_IAM include same-account versus cross-account identity/resource policies and effective denies. NONE removes IAM caller authentication but still requires the public resource-policy grants. Inspect lambda:InvokedViaFunctionUrl on InvokeFunction permission: a URL-only grant does not authorize direct Invoke. Handler tenant/object checks remain separate, and an intentionally public response is not a vulnerability.
controls.controlled_verification: Use an owned function with a synthetic response/action; compare intended caller and one restricted context without enumerating other functions.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: A public function URL or CORS header is not a vulnerability when only public content is returned.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Enforce the intended URL and handler authority, then retest legitimate invocation and restricted operations.
